chunks: And in the narration of Jamil, he said:

Regarding a man who divorces a young girl who has not reached puberty and one of her like does not conceive, though he had consummated marriage with her, and a woman who has despaired of menstruation, whose menses has ceased, and one of her like does not give birth, he said: There is no waiting period ('iddah) upon either of them.

key_terms.الصَّبِيَّةَ: the young girl who has not reached maturity
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: he consummated the marriage with her
key_terms.يَئِسَتْ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ: she has reached menopause and despaired of menstruation

ai.seo_question: Is there an 'iddah for a divorced prepubescent girl or a menopausal woman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning divorce for two categories of women: a prepubescent girl who is not of childbearing capacity, and a woman who has reached menopause and is no longer capable of bearing children. It rules that there is no 'iddah for either of them, even where consummation had occurred in the case mentioned.
